summary: Okanogan National Forest lookout known only from a site listing and a 1927 account that does not name the peak; no build date or present condition found.

events.note: Account dated August 1927 and signed H.T. Phelps, with Six Twenty-Six in parentheses; it describes an emergency lookout-fireman named Barren and does not name the peak

evidence.supports: Listing places the site in Okanogan National Forest
Six Twenty-Six appears in parentheses after the signature
Barren, an emergency lookout-fireman, returned from a fire on the head of Bridge Creek
evidence.quote: Barren, emergency lookout-fireman, had returned one evening from putting out a fire on the head of Bridge Creek.

evidence.supports: Lightning was striking all about the peak; the passage refers to the peak without naming it
evidence.quote: Lightning was striking viciously all about the peak

evidence.supports: Barren was taking off his wet shoes to turn in for the night
evidence.quote: preparatory to rolling in for the night

evidence.supports: Barren woke in the night with no memory of the interval
evidence.quote: Barren awoke some time during the night

evidence.supports: Barren woke in the night with no memory of the interval
evidence.quote: his recollections of the interlude zero

evidence.supports: His watch had stopped at 8:30 p.m.
evidence.quote: Upon looking at his watch he found it had stopped at 8:30 p.m.

notes_for_editor: Thinnest of the three. The only page on record is the Washington Lookouts listing: a survey location, the Okanogan National Forest heading and one 1927 passage credited to Six Twenty-Six. The passage never names the peak, so the link to Lincoln Butte is the listing's own. No build date, builder, design, staffing or present condition was found. Neither the firelookout.org county index nor the NHLR Washington list showed a Lincoln Butte entry in the copies read, and two web searches returned nothing specific. The brief's status and access are unknown; no correction proposed. Page reads went over the brief's budget of six (two 404s and register checks). Next step: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest heritage records or a newspaper search for Lincoln Butte.
